brief.what_it_is: Dungeon, also called Zork, is a text adventure game whose source code is in the public domain. The repository holds a C version of the mainframe game, converted from the FORTRAN source of Zork 2.6. You type commands at a prompt and the game replies with text describing the world. The README's startup banner, which appears in the fetched page, reads: "Welcome to Dungeon. This version created 11-MAR-91." It then shows the opening scene, a field west of a white house with a boarded front door.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the project's primary design goal is code preservation. It aims to keep the logic and behavior of the game as accurate as possible while updating the code to compile and run on modern C compilers and operating systems.
brief.how_it_works: The C code was generated from the f77 version with f2c, the FORTRAN-to-C translator, and then modified to remove the FORTRAN I/O library, add simple more processing, and change the format of the database file. The lineage runs from MDL (MUDDLE) at MIT, to DEC FORTRAN for the PDP-11 by Bob Supnik, to f77 on UNIX, and then to C. The README also notes that Dungeon differs from Zork I, which is a microcomputer adaptation covering about a third of the original map and puzzles.

entry.title: zork
entry.tldr: The public-domain mainframe Zork, called Dungeon, translated from FORTRAN to C so you can play the older, larger game on a modern terminal.
entry.deeper_look:
Dungeon, also known as Zork, is a text adventure. You type commands at a prompt and the game answers in prose. It opens in a field west of a white house with a boarded front door. This repository holds the C version of the mainframe game, converted from the FORTRAN source of Zork 2.6. The banner reads: "Welcome to Dungeon. This version created 11-MAR-91."

The README says the primary design goal is code preservation. The aim is to keep the game's logic and behavior as accurate as possible while letting the code compile and run on modern C compilers and operating systems. It is a museum piece that still runs, not a remake with new features.

The lineage is documented. The game began in MDL (MUDDLE) at MIT, went to DEC FORTRAN on the PDP-11 under Bob Supnik, then to f77 on UNIX, and then to C. The C code was generated with f2c, the FORTRAN-to-C translator, and then edited to remove the FORTRAN I/O library, add simple more processing, and change the format of the database file.

This is not the same game as Zork I. The README explains that Zork I is a microcomputer adaptation covering about a third of the original map and puzzles. In its words, "Dungeon represents the more complete, albeit earlier, mainframe experience." Playing it is a way into the history of interactive fiction, and of porting code across languages and decades.

entry.whats_unique: It is a machine-translated descendant of the original MIT mainframe game, with a documented chain from MDL to FORTRAN to f77 to C. It is the fuller Dungeon, not the shorter Zork I.
entry.caveats: It is a preservation project, so expect original behavior and no new features, and it is a different game from the better-known Zork I.
